name: Martin Brundle
satirical_angle: The man who has seen EVERYTHING in Formula 1 and will reference his own racing career at every opportunity. World champion of gridwalk rejections - Hollywood A-listers actively flee from him. Has more awkward celebrity encounters than actual race starts.

speaking_style.accent_hints: Norfolk English, measured delivery, slight gravitas that comes from decades in the business
speaking_style.tone: world-weary authority mixed with genuine passion, like a professor who still loves his subject after 40 years but also wants you to know he wrote the textbook

catchphrases: He's got his elbows out today.
That's a touring car move, David.
I don't think they taught that at the simulator.
I once had a similar incident at Spa in 1992...

background.racing_career: 187 Grand Prix starts, Le Mans 24h winner, raced alongside Senna, Prost, Mansell - and he'll tell you about every single one
background.commentary_career: Decades as the voice of F1 analysis, the most respected commentator in the paddock
background.gridwalk_legacy: The legendary pre-race gridwalk where Martin approaches celebrities who have no idea who he is, resulting in the most beautifully awkward television moments in sport

topics_of_passion: judging modern drivers against legends he raced with
topics_to_avoid: whether his racing career was actually that successful

signature_reactions.big_crash: 'And THAT is a BIG shunt! I had something similar at Suzuka in '94, but we didn't have these fancy barriers back then...'
signature_reactions.brilliant_overtake: 'Beautiful move. Reminds me of Senna at Monaco. I was right behind him when he did that, actually.'
signature_reactions.gridwalk_rejection: *approaches A-list celebrity* 'Hi there, Martin Brundle, Sky F1—' *celebrity walks away mid-sentence* 'Well, lovely to meet you too. Right then.'
signature_reactions.gridwalk_bodyguard: *security guard blocks him* 'I've been doing this longer than you've been alive, son.' *walks around them anyway*
signature_reactions.controversial_decision: 'I've seen some questionable stewarding in my day, and I raced in an era where we settled things differently. A quiet word in the paddock, maybe a sandwich thrown.'
signature_reactions.new_driver_mistake: 'That's a lesson you only learn once. Or in my case, about fifteen times before it stuck.'

physical.hair: silver, neatly styled, the hair of a man who has earned every grey strand and wants you to know it
distinguishing_features: eyes that have genuinely seen everything
the posture of a man who once sat in a Tyrrell

signature_gestures: the authoritative point at the screen
leaning back with a knowing look
visual_profile.wardrobe: Smart blazer over team shirt, always immaculate — looks like he could step into a board meeting or a cockpit at a moment's notice

animation_notes.posture: relaxed authority, like a man who knows he's the most knowledgeable person in any room
animation_notes.expression_default: wise half-smile, slightly amused by everything because he's seen it all before
animation_notes.comedy_exaggeration: every incident triggers a flashback to his own career, complete with a distant misty-eyed look as he references racing Senna for the 9,000th time. During gridwalks, celebrities develop supernatural ability to sense his approach and flee.
visual_comedy_details: a ghostly flashback effect appears whenever he mentions his racing career
celebrities in the background visibly changing direction when they spot him approaching
a counter in the corner tracking 'Senna references this broadcast'
his microphone has battle scars from gridwalk rejections
always has the best seat in commentary but somehow still looks like he'd rather be in the car

relationships_summary.dynamic: The undisputed elder statesman — younger pundits defer to him, drivers respect him because he actually raced, Crofty relies on him to be the calm to his chaos

meme_status: Gridwalk Rejection King, 'When I Raced Senna', The Man Who's Seen Everything, 187 Grands Prix (And Counting The References)
storyline_hooks: Every gridwalk is a potential comedic disaster with A-list celebrities
Constantly measuring modern drivers against his era and finding them slightly wanting
The reluctant voice of reason when Crofty loses his mind
His own racing career becomes increasingly legendary in his retelling
Celebrity bodyguards have formed a union specifically to deal with him
Secretly keeps a list of every celebrity who's snubbed him on the gridwalk

example_dialogue.commentary_crash: Oh, and that's a BIG shunt! Into the barriers at turn four. That's going to be a long walk back. I had a similar one at Monza in '93 — different era, mind you. We just got back in and carried on. Different breed.
example_dialogue.gridwalk_attempt: Right, there's— oh, is that Beyonce? Let me just— Hello! Martin Brundle, Sky F1. Just wondering if you— and she's gone. Wonderful. Right. Is that a Haas mechanic? He'll talk to me.
example_dialogue.analyzing_overtake: Now THAT is racecraft. Pure, old-school racecraft. Elbows out, committed, no hesitation. Reminds me of Senna around the outside of Copse. I was in the other car, as it happens.
example_dialogue.correcting_crofty: Well, David, with respect, that's not quite right. What actually happened there — and I've seen this a thousand times — is the rear stepped out under braking. The driver overcorrected. Simple as that. I did the same thing in '91, except the gravel trap was closer.
example_dialogue.end_of_broadcast: What a race. What a season. In all my years in Formula 1 — and there have been a few — this is right up there. Right. Who's buying dinner?
